title: Map managed permission policies into Agent Host sessions
body:
## Summary

Adds a reusable bridge from explicitly configured VS Code settings to Copilot SDK `managedSettings.permissions` for Agent Host sessions.

The bridge is declarative: each mapping selects a VS Code setting and provides a typed callback that transforms its effective configured value into a managed-permissions contribution. The first two mappings are:

| VS Code setting | Effective configured value | SDK managed setting contribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.tools.global.autoApprove` | `false` | `disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` |
| `chat.tools.terminal.enableAutoApprove` | `false` | `ask: ["Shell"]` |

Untouched defaults do not create managed settings. Explicit values from policy, application, user, workspace, workspace-folder, or memory scopes use normal VS Code precedence and are eligible for mapping.

## Design

- `createManagedPermissionsSettingMapping(settingId, transform)` is the extension point for future mappings.
- `resolveManagedPermissions(configurationService)` evaluates all mappings and combines their restrictive contributions.
- Agent Host forwarding and **Developer: Policy Diagnostics** consume the same resolver.
- The renderer forwards the resulting root-config value; the Agent Host passes it to SDK session create and resume as `managedSettings.permissions`.
- VS Code does not probe runtime capabilities or decide whether the settings are enforceable. Validation, composition, and enforcement belong to the SDK/runtime.
- The empty object is retained as the JSON-safe clear sentinel and normalized before SDK launch.

## Lifecycle and safety

- Applies the same managed settings to create and resume.
- Refreshes default and peer-chat SDK sessions before the next turn when the effective settings change.
- Sends renderer-owned config before restored authentication, subscriptions, and pending turn replay after a fresh-initialize reconnect fallback.
- Combines contributions restrictively across connected clients.
- Retains a disconnected client's contribution through reconnect grace, then removes it without allowing a delayed queued update to recreate stale state.
- Invalidates only stale queued managed-permission updates; unrelated accepted client actions continue normally.
- Keeps the value transient rather than persisting it in Agent Host root configuration storage.
- Redacts `managedPermissions` from AHP JSONL and Agent Service trace logs without changing the wire payload.

## Scope

Permissions only. This does not add sandbox-floor mapping, network policy mapping, or generic per-tool eligibility. Permissive values do not synthesize `allow` rules.

## Validation

title: Use native TypeScript for layer checker
body:
## Summary

Migrate the custom semantic layer checker from the JavaScript TypeScript compiler API to the unstable native TypeScript API exposed by `@typescript/native/unstable/sync`.

This is an exploratory follow-up to [#327942](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327942) and [#327953](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327953). It keeps the six existing layer-specific `tsc` checks unchanged and moves only the custom semantic rule check to the native compiler.

## Motivation

Even after reducing semantic symbol lookups in [#327953](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327953), the JavaScript compiler still keeps the full TypeScript program and semantic graph in the Node heap. The native API lets the Go compiler own that graph while Node fetches and traverses source ASTs one file at a time.

This significantly reduces Node heap pressure and removes the need for the layer checker's 8 GB Node heap allowance.

## Implementation

- Open a native TypeScript snapshot for a dedicated semantic-check tsconfig.
- Exclude test and fixture roots in that tsconfig.
- Fetch one matching source AST at a time.
- Collect direct-name, alias, and property-member candidates locally.
- Resolve all candidates for a file in one batched native checker call.
- Follow aliases with `getAliasedSymbol` and containing symbols with `Symbol.getParent`.
- Clear the Node-side source-file cache after each file.
- Scope `GOMEMLIMIT=4GiB` to the spawned native compiler and restore the caller's environment afterward.
- Dispose the snapshot and API client on every exit path.

The existing behavior remains covered:

| Usage shape | Detection |
| --- | --- |
| Direct forbidden type | Exact-name candidate and native symbol lookup |
| Renamed import/export | Alias collection and `getAliasedSymbol` |
| Member of inferred forbidden type | Property-access candidate and `Symbol.getParent` |
| Raw `ipcMain` access | Exact/property-access candidate |
| Skipped tests and fixtures | Excluded from roots; skip rule remains defensive for imports |

## Performance

Measurements were taken on the same source tree and machine. RSS values are peak resident memory sampled across the checker process tree.

| Implementation | Runtime | Node RSS | Native Go RSS | Combined RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Optimized JavaScript checker ([#327953](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327953)) | ~23s | ~3.79 GiB | n/a | ~3.79 GiB |
| Native checker, unconstrained Go heap | ~14s | ~0.55 GiB | ~4.11 GiB | ~4.66 GiB |
| **Native checker, `GOMEMLIMIT=4GiB` (this PR)** | **~18s** | **~0.51 GiB** | **~3.56 GiB** | **~4.06 GiB** |
| Native checker, `GOMEMLIMIT=2500MiB` | ~32s | ~0.50 GiB | ~2.50 GiB | ~3.01 GiB |

The selected 4 GiB limit reduces Node RSS by roughly 3.28 GiB and improves runtime by roughly 5 seconds versus the optimized JavaScript checker. Combined RSS is roughly 280 MiB higher than the JavaScript implementation, but remains roughly 600 MiB below unconstrained native TypeScript.

Without `GOMEMLIMIT`, the migration mostly moves memory from Node to Go and increases combined RSS, so the scoped Go limit is an essential part of this change.

## Correctness verification

In addition to unit tests, I mutation-tested the production checker by temporarily adding two real violations under `src/`:

- an aliased `IMainProcessService` used from browser code
- raw `electron.ipcMain` used outside the validated wrapper

The native checker exited with code 1 and reported both violations, including alias references and source locations. After removing the mutation files, the full layer suite passed again.

## Stability consideration

The native API is explicitly exported under `@typescript/native/unstable`. This PR intentionally remains draft so we can evaluate whether the memory/runtime gains justify depending on that API. The native package itself is already a repository dependency; this does not add a new package.

## Validation

- `node --test build/lib/test/layersChecker.test.ts`
- `npm --prefix build test -- --test-name-pattern='layersChecker'` (239 tests)
- `npm --prefix build run typecheck`
- `node build/eslint.ts build/checker/layersChecker.ts build/lib/test/layersChecker.test.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- real-source mutation test for aliased native services and raw `ipcMain`
- `npm run precommit`
- focused code review: no significant findings

(Written by Copilot)

title: Fix replayed text doubling and split the overloaded Codex E2E gate
body:
Three findings from actually running the gated Codex scenarios rather than trusting the inventory. Two of them turned out to be different from what `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` recorded.

## The replayed text doubling was ours, not the provider's

The doc attributed a family of Codex failures to the provider duplicating response content. It reproduces exactly — a recorded `SHELL_VALUE_73` replays as `SHELL_VALUE_73SHELL_VALUE_73` — but the cause is in our own SSE regenerator.

`responsesMessageToSse` announced each output item via `response.output_item.added` with the item's **final content already attached**, then streamed that same text as deltas. A consumer that accumulates both counts it twice. An announced item now arrives empty, which is what the event means.

Recording proxies real CAPI bytes and was never affected — which is exactly why the recorded capture looked correct while the replayed snapshot did not, and why this survived so long.

Found by bisecting the regenerator's events one at a time; four other candidates (`content_part.done`, `output_item.done`, `output_text.done`, `response.completed`) were eliminated first.

## Codex has no file tools

Its captures contain only `exec_command`; Claude's contain `Read`, `Write`, `Bash`.

The shared file-operation prompts steer the agent away from the shell (`Use your file tools; do not run a shell command.`) so captures stay platform-neutral. Codex cannot satisfy that and does not fall back:

```
I can't access file contents without using a shell command in this environment,
and you asked me not to run one.
```

`counts lines in a file` shows the sharper version: it flails and answers `3` for a four-line file. This is a capability difference, not something re-recording fixes — which is why the previous entry ("no fixture recorded → record it") could never have worked.

## The gate conflated three things

`stableNewScenarioResponse` meant "replays unstably" *and* "never recorded" *and* "cannot run this at all". `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` already said splitting it was a prerequisite for reducing it.

It is replaced by `supportsFileTools`. `retains context across consecutive turns` — which involves no files and no tools, and was only ever caught by the same overloaded flag — now runs for Codex.

## Result

Codex **8 → 9 passing**, stable across repeated runs. Conformance 57, Copilot 49, Claude 44, 0 failing; 2683 unit tests pass.

A modest test-count win on purpose. I enabled the six shell-based scenarios first and measured: the suite then failed about one run in four, with the failing scenario **moving between runs** — the shared-server load ceiling, not a fault in any one test. Rather than ship that, they stay gated with the real reason recorded, and `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` now names what has to be understood before they can be enabled.

(Written by Copilot)

title: GitHub Copilot `file_search` truncation can cause false “file does not exist” conclusions
body:
GitHub Copilot `file_search` result truncation consistently trips up models. **This is a recurring problem and the results misguide models.** A model such as GPT-5.6 Luna is completely capable of a simple task of loading the context window with relevant context. However if there are many files, the `file_search` tool just truncates results and **does not provide sufficient notice to the model that results were truncated and that more results are available**. Instead, the model comes away with the impression that some of the files it was looking for does not exist.

Below is the explanation in the words of GPT-5.6 Sol:

# `file_search` truncation is not reported explicitly enough

## Description

A prompt requested loading several project-context artifacts, including an active work item's description, while skipping targets that do not exist.

I searched the work item's directory using a recursive glob:

```text
path/to/work-item/**
```

I omitted `maxResults`, expecting the returned file list to be sufficient for determining which requested artifacts existed.

The tool reported the total number of matches, displayed only a subset, and ended the output with `...`. Because truncation was indicated only by this unstructured ellipsis, the omitted description file was incorrectly treated as absent.

A targeted search or a sufficiently large `maxResults` returns the file correctly, so this is not an indexing failure. It is a result-reporting problem: callers can easily mistake a partial result set for a complete inventory.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a directory containing more files than `file_search` displays by default.
2. Place the target file outside the subset selected for display.
3. Call `file_search` with a recursive glob and omit `maxResults`.
4. Observe that the tool reports the total match count, displays only some paths, and appends `...`.
5. Observe that the response provides no structured truncation flag, displayed-result count, or continuation mechanism.

## Actual Behavior

Truncation is represented only by a trailing ellipsis. A matching file omitted from the displayed subset can therefore be mistaken for a nonexistent file.

## Expected Behavior

The response should explicitly state that it is truncated, for example:

```text
Showing 20 of 24 results. Results truncated; narrow the query or increase maxResults.
```

Ideally the tool result would also expose structured metadata such as:

```json
{
  "totalResults": 24,
  "returnedResults": 20,
  "truncated": true
}
```

This would let agents reliably distinguish “no match exists” from “the match may have been omitted.”

## Environment

agentHost: fix side chats from reconnected and server-initiated turns
body:
Fixes side chats (`/btw`, selection side chats, **Ask in Side Chat**) failing with:

```
[AgentService] createChat: side chat source turn request_<uuid> not found in ahp-chat://default/...
```

## Root cause

The renderer minted a client-side `request_<uuid>` id for turns it did not dispatch itself, so the side-chat anchor referenced a turn the agent host had never heard of. The `request_` prefix is the tell — that's `ChatRequestModel` generating an id because no `restoredId` was supplied.

Two paths dropped the provider's turn id:

1. **Reconnect/restore** — the active turn was pushed into `history` without an `id`, while completed turns got `id: turn.id` from `turnsToHistory`. So reloading the window mid-turn (or reconnecting to an in-flight turn) rebased the anchor onto a synthetic id.
2. **Server-initiated turns** — `IChatSessionServerRequest` carried no turn id at all, and `chatServiceImpl` passed `undefined /* id */` to `model.addRequest`.

This is why it looked intermittent: when the turn was dispatched by *this* client and never reloaded, the client request id *is* the turn id, so it worked.

Same broken anchor also affected forking off an in-flight turn.

## Fix

Plumb the provider turn id through both paths, and make it **required** rather than optional so it cannot be silently omitted again — an absent id is precisely the defect, since the consumer then quietly mints one the host can never resolve.

- `chatSessionsService.ts` — `IChatSessionServerRequest.id: string`
- `chatServiceImpl.ts` — forward it as the request's `restoredId`
- `agentHostSessionHandler.ts` — `startServerRequest` takes `turnId` as a required positional parameter; set `id` on the reconnect history item

`IChatSessionHistoryItem.id` stays optional — extension-contributed sessions legitimately may not have stable turn ids for historical requests. Only the live server-turn path needed tightening.

## Validation

- `typecheck-client` clean for touched files; hygiene clean
- Unit tests: `AgentHostChatContribution` (272), `ChatService` (73), `ChatModel` (126), side-chat suites (33)
- Two existing tests tightened to snapshot-style assertions covering the ids, plus a new `ChatService` test asserting the host turn id is adopted

title: chat: replace the dictation shimmer with a static processing color
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8613

While dictating, the in-progress transcript animated a gradient shimmer over the words the recognizer had not committed yet. This renders that text in the input placeholder color instead — no animation, just a flat provisional color that turns solid when dictation ends.

### Behavior

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| In-progress transcript | animated shimmer | **placeholder color, static** |
| Final transcript | solid | solid (unchanged) |

The terminal voice surface gets the same treatment, so the chat input, editor, and terminal dictation surfaces stay consistent.

### Why the heuristics went away

The shimmer needed a stopping condition, otherwise the last word would loop forever while you paused mid-sentence. That required three supporting pieces: an interim-diff comparison, a word-boundary backoff, and a 700ms idle-settle timer. None of them are needed once nothing animates, so they're gone.

### A CSS specificity trap worth knowing about

The first attempt at this looked correct but rendered nothing — dictation appeared to jump straight from empty to the finished transcript. The decoration was being applied on every update; it simply had no visual effect:

| classes on the span | computed color |
| --- | --- |
| `mtk1` (Monaco token) | `rgb(32,32,32)` |
| `dictation-interim-processing` | `rgb(153,153,153)` |
| **both together (the real case)** | **`rgb(32,32,32)` — token won** |

`.monaco-editor .dictation-interim-processing` ties on specificity with Monaco's `.monaco-editor .mtkN` token rules, which are injected into the document *after* the static stylesheet and therefore win the tie.

The old shimmer never hit this because it colored text through `-webkit-text-fill-color` and `background-clip: text`, which bypass `color` entirely — the pre-existing `.dictation-interim-settled` rule had the same latent bug, masked by the animation. The selector is now qualified as `.monaco-editor .view-line span.dictation-interim-processing` so it outranks the token rules regardless of injection order.

Worth flagging for reviewers because unit tests cannot catch this class of bug: the decoration-range assertions passed throughout. It only shows up in a real editor with themed tokens.

### Notes for reviewers

- `LiveTranscriptInserter` now keeps a single decorations collection instead of two; `clearShimmer()` → `clearInterimDecorations()`.
- Added a test pinning that the in-progress region carries the decoration and that it clears on finalization. The duplicated service mock across tests is factored into a helper.
- Verified with `gulp compile-client` (no errors in the touched files) and `./scripts/test.sh --grep DictationSession` (4/4, including the `continues dictating after the user edits the transcript` test added upstream in #327832, which this merge preserves).

Net −181 lines across the touched files.

title: telemetry: report ResizeObserver delivery context
body:
## Problem

VS Code currently rewrites Chromium's stackless `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` warning with the name of the **most recently invoked** `DisposableResizeObserver`:

```ts
_lastInvokedDisposableResizeObserver = this;
```

The telemetry comments call that observer the "offending consumer," but callback order is not causality. A callback can mutate a different observed target, and an unrelated observer can run last before the browser dispatches the warning. This is how a real cross-observer virtualized-row lifecycle bug was attributed to both `ChatInputPart.containerHeight` and `ChatListItemRenderer.itemHeight`.

The browser cannot provide the missing answer after the fact. Per the ResizeObserver processing model, skipped targets stay in internal `[[skippedTargets]]`; `Deliver Resize Loop Error` creates an `ErrorEvent` with only the generic message. No observer, target, or causative callback is exposed to JavaScript.

## Change

Replace false causal attribution with honest delivery context:

```text
[ResizeObserverLoopContext(A,B)]
```

- records every distinct wrapped observer that ran in the current rendering frame;
- scopes state per `CodeWindow`, because auxiliary windows have independent documents and delivery loops;
- sorts names so callback order does not fragment equivalent buckets;
- bounds context to the lexicographically smallest 8 names plus `<overflow>` so output is deterministic and finite;
- clears at the next animation frame, after Blink has dispatched any loop warning from the current rendering update;
- keeps the `ResizeObserverLoopContext` wrapper as the explicit non-causal label.

Only `DisposableResizeObserver` consumers are included; raw `ResizeObserver` consumers remain outside this context.

This changes the bucket shape on purpose. Existing per-last-callback buckets should not be interpreted as component failure rates.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passes.
- `scripts/test.bat --grep "DisposableResizeObserver"` — 10 passing:
  - synchronous delivery remains unchanged;
  - names are sorted and deduplicated;
  - overflow is canonical even when callbacks arrive in reverse order;
  - state is isolated per window;
  - state clears at the next animation frame.
- New real Chromium component fixture deliberately resizes its own observed target. Playwright asserts the browser-generated loop warning still sees:

```text
[ResizeObserverLoopContext(ResizeObserverContextFixture.selfResizer)]
```

The fixture stops observation on the first warning so it cannot leak or spin.
- Independent code review: no significant issues.

## Follow-up

This PR makes the cheap signal truthful; it does **not** claim to recover exact causality. A separate sampled diagnostic can trace callback → changed observed-target geometry/connectivity edges after the first warning. That work needs coverage/confidence gates and should not be mixed into the stable error bucket change.

Related: #293359, #316509, #316501, #327933.

title: Improve dictation list formatting with explicit ordering cues
body:
## Description

Dictated speech was rarely formatted as a Markdown list — enumerations came out as paragraphs even when the user clearly spoke a sequence of steps or items.

The `final` list guidance in `createDictationCleanupSystemPrompt` was too vague ("format it as a Markdown bulleted or numbered list, choosing numbered only when order matters") for the cleanup model to act on reliably.

- **Stronger, cue-driven list instruction**: Rewrote the `listInstruction` for the `final` source to trigger on "two or more items, steps, or options", emit one item per line, and pick a numbered list when the wording implies order — ordinals (`first`, `second`, `third`, `next`, `finally`), counting (`one`, `two`, `three`), or `step one`/`step two`. Bulleted (`-`) otherwise, with an explicit guard against inventing items.

```
When the speaker enumerates two or more items, steps, or options, format them as a
Markdown list with one item per line instead of a paragraph. Use a numbered list when
the wording implies order or sequence (for example ordinals like "first", "second",
"third", "next", "finally", counting like "one", "two", "three", or phrases like
"step one" or "step two"); otherwise use a bulleted list with "-". Do not add items
the speaker did not dictate.
```

- **Incremental behavior unchanged**: The live partial (`incremental`) transcript still omits list formatting to avoid premature restructuring while the user is speaking.
- **Test**: Added a unit test asserting the list/numbered guidance is present for `final` and absent for `incremental`.

title: fix: guard null visibleRangeForPosition in indent guides (fixes #244370)
body:
### Summary
The indent guides view part crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'left')` inside `IndentGuidesOverlay.prepareRender`. The code calls `ctx.visibleRangeForPosition(...)!.left`, using a non-null assertion (`!`) on a value whose declared type is `HorizontalPosition | null`. When the position is not currently laid out (e.g. during rendering transitions, wrapped/hidden lines, or GPU-render fallbacks), `visibleRangeForPosition` legitimately returns `null` and the `!` bypasses the nullable contract, throwing.

Notably, two sibling calls in the *same* function already handle the nullable return correctly with `?.left ?? fallback` (the `leftOffset` computation and the horizontal-line `width` computation). Only the per-guide `left` computation used `!`, making it the sole unguarded consumer of the same nullable API.

Fixes microsoft/vscode\#244370
Recommended reviewer: `@hediet`

### Culprit Commit
`78cb0b490a60` by `@hediet` (2022-04-01) introduced the `left` computation with the `!` non-null assertion on `ctx.visibleRangeForPosition(...)`. The method's return type has been `HorizontalPosition | null` throughout, so the assertion was a type-contract bypass from the start; the null branch only manifests under specific viewport/layout states, which is why it surfaces as intermittent telemetry rather than a deterministic crash.

### Code Flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[view.ts render loop] --> B[ViewOverlays.prepareRender]
  B --> C[IndentGuidesOverlay.prepareRender]
  C --> D[loop over guides]
  D --> E["ctx.visibleRangeForPosition(pos)"]
  E -->|returns null when position not laid out| F["!.left throws TypeError"]
```

### Affected Files
- `src/vs/editor/browser/viewParts/indentGuides/indentGuides.ts` — the crash site and the fix.
- `src/vs/editor/browser/view/renderingContext.ts` — declares `visibleRangeForPosition(position: Position): HorizontalPosition | null` (unchanged; confirms the nullable contract).

### Repro Steps
Not reliably reproducible on demand — the null return depends on transient viewport/layout state (line not currently rendered, wrapping, or GPU vs DOM line-rendering fallback) while indent guides are enabled. The fix is derived from the deminified stack and the declared nullable contract rather than a manual repro.

### How the Fix Works
**Chosen approach** (`indentGuides.ts`): replace the non-null assertion `)!.left` with optional chaining `)?.left`, making `left` typed `number | undefined`, then add an explicit `if (left === undefined) { continue; }` guard before `left` is used. Because the declared type is *already* nullable (`HorizontalPosition | null`), handling the null at this site is the correct, contract-honoring fix — this is not a crash-site guard masking an upstream producer, since `visibleRangeForPosition` is a documented nullable renderer API whose null is an expected 'position not currently visible' signal (the two sibling calls in this same function already treat it that way). `continue` (rather than `break`) skips only the single non-renderable guide and still renders the remaining guides on the line, preserving the existing behavior where a guide beyond the viewport is simply not drawn.

**Alternatives considered**: fall back to `leftOffset` or `0` when null — rejected because an arbitrary horizontal position would render a visibly misplaced guide; skipping the guide matches the surrounding code's intent (guides past `scrollWidth`/`_maxIndentLeft` are already dropped).

### Recommended Owner
`@hediet` — author of the culprit commit `78cb0b490a60`, owner of the editor indent-guides area, and already assigned to the issue.

body:
Follow up to #326766 and #324136. PR #327947 adds persistent user/workspace auto-approve actions to Agent Host Copilot terminal confirmations, but there is still a parser mismatch for the SDK's `powershell` tool.

The workbench generates suggestions using the PowerShell tree-sitter grammar, while Agent Host's `commandAutoApprover.ts` only loads `tree-sitter-bash.wasm` for eligibility and enforcement.

Impact:

- **Existing settings rule:** a simple rule such as `"Get-ChildItem": true` usually works because bash can treat it as a generic command name. Rules for PowerShell-specific syntax can still miss because Agent Host splits/interprets the command using bash grammar.
- **Rule added from #327947:** the workbench can suggest and persist a rule from an accurate PowerShell parse, but Agent Host re-parses the next command as bash. The user selects "Always Allow" and is prompted again.
- **Exact command-line rule:** this can also miss when bash parsing fails because Agent Host parses before checking the exact command-line allow rule.

Representative cases include pipelines with script blocks (`Where-Object { ... }`), `$()` subexpressions, backtick continuations, PowerShell operators, and PowerShell-specific redirects such as `$null`.

The expected failure mode is conservative re-prompting/inconsistent suggestions; Agent Host remains authoritative for approval. There is no known auto-approval bypass from this mismatch.

Work needed:

- Load `tree-sitter-powershell.wasm` in the Agent Host command auto-approver (it already ships in the same package).
- Carry/select the shell grammar for both rule eligibility and enforcement.
- Add coverage for existing settings rules and rules created from #327947, including PowerShell-specific sub-command and exact-command-line cases.

Related forwarding work: #322774.

title: Keep chat input visible when enabling voice mode with an existing prompt
Fix dictation getting stuck on when transcript cleanup stalls
body:
## Description

Dictation could get stuck "on" and stop responding to clicks and the keybinding when the network was flaky, accompanied by `[chat-stt] language model transcript cleanup failed (source=incremental, reason=cancelled); using raw transcript Error: network request aborted` in the console.

On stop, `stopAndTranscribe()` runs a final language-model cleanup pass (`_cleanupWithLanguageModel`) that consumes the model response:

```ts
for await (const part of response.stream) { ... }
await response.result;
```

A 10s timer cancels the token, but cancellation was only observed *between* stream chunks and `response.result` was awaited unconditionally. A half-open request (never yields another chunk, never errors, never completes) therefore never resolved — wedging `stopAndTranscribe()`, the promise that stop/toggle and Escape await, so dictation stayed in the transcribing state indefinitely.

- **Bound the consumption**: wrapped the `stream` + `result` consumption in `raceCancellation(..., cts.token)` — the same token the timeout timer and `cancel()` already drive. A stalled request now can't outlast the timeout; cleanup falls back to the raw transcript and the session tears down to `Idle`, keeping stop/cancel responsive.

Behavior is otherwise unchanged: error → raw-transcript fallback, empty/refusal handling, and cancellation logging are preserved. The same cleanup path is used for incremental (during recording) and final (on stop) cleanup, so both are now bounded.

title: Route web Voice Mode through agent hosts
body:
## Summary

- remove direct Voice backend endpoint forwarding to web clients
- relay web Voice Mode traffic through the connected Agent Host Service and code tunnel
- authenticate the host-side Voice WebSocket with the Agent Host token
- preserve the direct Voice transport for native clients
- bound and redact relayed payloads, and recover across pending connections and tunnel reconnects

This replaces the unsupported direct-browser approach from #327409. Web Voice Mode now follows the Agent Host architecture: run a code tunnel on a host, then connect from `vscode.dev/agents`.

Fixes to #327310.

## How to test

1. On an authenticated host, run:
   ```bash
   code tunnel --accept-server-license-terms --name voice-ahs-test
   ```
2. Sign into `https://vscode.dev/agents` with the same account and connect to `voice-ahs-test`.
3. Start Voice Mode, grant microphone permission, speak, and verify transcription and narrated responses.
4. In browser DevTools, verify no browser WebSocket connects directly to the Voice backend; Voice traffic should use the Agent Host tunnel.
5. Stop Voice Mode and verify audio/events stop, then start it again successfully.
6. Start Voice Mode and immediately stop it while it is connecting; verify no phantom session remains, then start it again.
7. While Voice Mode is active, stop the tunnel, wait beyond the first reconnect attempt, restart the same tunnel command, and verify Voice Mode reconnects automatically.
8. Speak again after recovery and verify transcription and narrated responses, then disconnect cleanly.

title: Fix hold-to-talk for Voice Mode push-to-talk keybinding
body:
## Description

Holding the Voice Mode push-to-talk keybinding (`Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Space`) to speak didn't work and produced a glitchy start/stop flicker; only a quick tap enabled speak mode. This brings Voice Mode PTT in line with how chat dictation implements hold-to-talk.

**Root cause:** `agentsVoice.pushToTalk` only called `pttDown()` and never enabled keybinding hold-mode, so:
- The keybinding service re-dispatched the command on every OS key-repeat while held → the visual flicker.
- Release depended entirely on the widget's DOM key-tracking, so a held press often never finished the turn.

**Changes** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/agentsVoice/browser/agentsVoice.contribution.ts`):
- Enable `enableKeybindingHoldMode('agentsVoice.pushToTalk')` **synchronously before any `await`**, matching `agentsVoice.startVoiceInChat` and dictation. This also makes the keybinding service swallow OS key-repeat while held, removing the flicker.
- The command now owns release: `pttDown()` on press, `await holdMode` then `pttUp()` on key-up, so a real hold records while held and finishes the turn on release.
- When invoked without a held key (command palette / programmatic), emulate a tap so the controller enters toggle mode.

```ts
const holdMode = keybindingService.enableKeybindingHoldMode('agentsVoice.pushToTalk');
// ...connect if needed...
voiceController.pttDown();
if (!holdMode) { voiceController.pttUp(); return; } // tap → toggle
await holdMode;
voiceController.pttUp();                              // release → finish turn
```

The widget's existing DOM key-tracking is left in place as a harmless fallback (`pttUp()` is guarded by `_pttHeld`).

> Note: the issue thread is contradictory — the agent instructions ask to add PTT "just like chat dictation," while a later comment says "Not going to support this." This implements the former; happy to drop it if that's the final call.

title: Skip voice narration summary for cancelled chat turns
body:
## Description

In voice mode, cancelling an in-progress turn narrated a summary of the partial work — reading back operations the user deliberately chose to stop.

When a request is cancelled, the response's `isIncomplete` flag flips to `false`, so `VoiceSessionController._getAgentStateInfo` treated it as a normal `idle` completion and built a `last_response_summary` from the partial response markdown, which was then sent to the backend and narrated.

### Changes

- **`voiceSessionController.ts`**: In `_getAgentStateInfo`, after the `thinking` check, return `{ state: 'idle' }` with no `last_response_summary` when `lastRequest.response.isCanceled` is true. The session still transitions to idle; there's just nothing to narrate.

  ```ts
  if (lastRequest?.response?.isCanceled) {
      return { state: 'idle' };
  }
  ```

  This complements the existing `markUserCancelled` suppression (which only covers the cancel gesture from the voice widget) by also handling cancellations from other surfaces, e.g. the chat panel Stop button.

- **`voiceSessionController.test.ts`**: Added coverage asserting a cancelled response yields `{ state: 'idle' }` with no summary; extended the `completedResponseModel` helper with an `isCanceled` flag.

title: Only show "Downloading model" for dictation on an actual cache miss
body:
## Description

Starting on-device dictation flashed "Downloading model" the first time per window/workspace, even though the model is downloaded once and cached under the shared per-user `cacheHome`. The model was never re-downloaded — each window runs its own fresh utility-process `LocalTranscriptionService` instance, and `_ensureModel` emitted the `Downloading` status *before* checking `model.isCached`, so the spurious download UI appeared once per instance.

Changes in `LocalTranscriptionService._ensureModel`:

- Report `Loading` while the native runtime, SDK, and manager are prepared and the catalog is queried — the cache state is unknown at that point.
- Emit `Downloading` (progress 0) only inside the `if (!model.isCached)` branch, once a genuine cache miss is confirmed, so real first-time downloads still surface progress promptly.

Subsequent workspaces, where the model is already cached on disk, now go `Loading → Ready` with no download UI. True first-ever downloads are unchanged.

## Dictation icon now tracks the real prepare state

Previously the "preparing" affordance chose its glyph off the backend *name* (`currentBackend === 'mai'`), so the on-device (nemo) backend always showed the download-mic while preparing — even when it was only loading an already-cached model. The distinction between `Downloading` and `Loading` was invisible to the UI because both collapsed into `isPreparingModel`.

- Added an `isDownloadingModel` signal (with `onDidChangeDownloadingModel`) to `IChatSpeechToTextService`, set to `true` only while the service reports the `Downloading` model state (a confirmed cache miss).
- All three dictation surfaces now key their glyph off this state instead of the backend name:
  - **Chat toolbar button** (`DictationDownloadActionViewItem`, Voice Mode off)
  - **Voice/dictation pill** (`voiceInputModeActionViewItem`, Voice Mode on)
  - **Agents window mic** (`newChatInput`)
- While preparing, each surface shows the **download-mic + determinate progress ring** only during an actual download, and a **spinning loading glyph** otherwise (loading a cached model into memory). The pill now wraps its download glyph in the same `DictationDownloadRing` used by the toolbar button so all three read identically.

Resulting behavior, consistent across normal and Agents windows:

- **Nemo (on-device):** download-mic + ring while downloading (cache miss) → spinner while loading → mic when ready.
- **MAI (cloud):** spinner throughout (it connects but never downloads a model, so `isDownloadingModel` stays `false`).

The spin animation now also applies when Voice Mode is disabled.

No test is added for `_ensureModel`: it dynamically imports the native `foundry-local-sdk` addon and has no injection seam, so covering it would require a non-minimal refactor. The icon/state wiring is covered by the existing dictation and voice-input-mode unit tests.

title: Reset voice mode when a fresh new-session composer takes over (agents window)
body:
In the agents window, enabling Voice Mode in a new-session view, creating a session by voice, then opening another new session (`Cmd+N`) left the new composer showing Voice Mode as enabled while it couldn't actually be talked to — clicking merely fell back to the toggle button.

## Description

Voice Mode is a global singleton bound to the surface that started it. When a fresh welcome composer becomes the active voice surface, the still-open connection remains bound to the previous surface and can't route to the new composer — but because `isConnected` is global, the new composer's toolbar/pill rendered the connected chrome regardless.

- **`SessionsVoiceNewComposerContribution`** (new, in `voiceBridge.contribution.ts`): watches the active new-chat composer and disconnects a connected voice session when a *different welcome composer* takes over, so the new view starts from a clean, off state.
  - Tracks the owning composer across the transient `undefined` gap (old composer disposed before the next mounts) to distinguish a genuine surface change from churn, and to avoid disconnecting a composer against itself.
  - In-session composers (`routesWhileSessionActive`) intentionally keep routing an active session's voice and are exempt.
- Added focused unit tests covering: disconnect on a fresh welcome composer, no disconnect when switching to a routing in-session composer, and no disconnect while idle.
